Visual sandbox only. No edits are saved.

Keep the warmth. Add a quiet note.

Cream, coral and amber stay central. The selected sage tone is a low-saturation supporting surface for consent context. It never signals consent by color alone and never changes the four phase meanings.

Warm paper#F9F3ED
Coral action#A53D30
Amber light#E4B86F
Quiet sage#4C6753
Night ink#0E1020
Editorial type, useful scale

DM Serif Display for page and phase headings; DM Sans for controls, body and tabular dates. Native implementation bundles fonts after approval. Forms keep native input semantics and unrestricted font scaling.

Glass where it earns its place

One detached dock with a sliding selected thumb. A low-opacity tint, native content blur, reflective rim and a shallow warm shadow. Opaque controls and text surfaces keep contrast stable. Reduced transparency and older Android get a solid surface.

Room for thumbs and text

4-point spacing. 16–24-point gutters. At least 48-point actions. The content viewport ends above the dock; long pages keep scrolling. Large text reflows vertically and expands navigation height; at 200% the mockup uses two columns to keep full dock labels readable.

Motion with a job

Native dock thumb: spring motion on the UI thread. Press feedback: 120–180ms. No decorative loops. Reduced motion removes movement. Keyboard-aware native forms keep the focused field and Save visible.

Existing web artwork is reused. The sage tone is selected; native contrast remains to be qualified. Browser scaling is a layout stress preview; it does not prove Android font scaling, TalkBack, performance or native keyboard behavior.

Single consolidated final Android QA checklist

NOT RUN. Run once on the complete, accepted final stack head after native implementation. Reuse the approved persistent synthetic primary/partner pair and isolated backend. Record exact source/APK/device identity and PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT RUN per scenario. Browser mockups and CI do not count.

  1. Primary and partner onboarding, initial exact/approximate date, cycle/period bounds, interruption/resume, partial write and offline failure.
  2. Period start/end, correction, explicit deletion confirmation under allowed policy, pain/tags/private note privacy, combined timeline/provenance, web↔Android refresh and consent-aware CSV cleanup.
  3. Pairing valid/invalid/expired code, copy/share, nickname privacy, connected-since date, date cancel, revocation, replacement-partner sharing restrictions and primary calendar selection.
  4. Private chat unread/older pages, quick lines/emoji, reactions, delivery/read receipts, clear cancel/confirm, stale relationship generation, offline and failed writes.
  5. Default-off inbox with no subscription; enabled synthetic inbox read/dismiss/load more and destinations, reminder local time in account timezone; no push claim.
  6. Settings lengths, name/gender/relationship term, Light/System/Dark, pause/private context/sharing, failure draft retention; exact accepted concurrency contract on web↔Android changes.
  7. In-place A→B account switch with equal and unequal baselines, logout/login, revoked sessions, reconnect and no prior-account drafts, cache, health or chat disclosure.
  8. Compact and large Android layouts, light/dark, 100/130/200% fonts, TalkBack reading/focus order, selected-state labels, 48dp targets, contrast over all surfaces and four phases, reduced motion, opaque fallback, keyboard/date picker and full scrolling.
  9. Native privacy shield before sensitive content, screenshot/Recents behavior, clipboard expiry/cleanup and app background/foreground. Record emulator versus physical-device limits separately.

Log failures under CB-01–CB-06 owning feature tickets, fix there, rerun targeted checks, then accept the stack bottom-up into gate5/atlas-foundation. This pass does not authorize production deployment.

Design sources, skills and native implementation boundaries

Source of truth: app/globals.css, docs/cb-connect-design-guidelines.md, mobile theme/tokens.ts, existing feature components and public DTOs. Existing phase artwork is reused rather than inventing a separate visual identity.

  • Redesign, Hallmark, design taste, visual foundations, high-end design and minimalist skills inform hierarchy, restrained material, type and token consistency.
  • Native/iOS/Android, responsive, interaction, design-system and accessibility skills inform safe areas, large targets, keyboard/focus, scaling and reduced motion. Generic landing-page effects, framework changes and palette replacement are excluded.
  • Expo SDK 57 docs confirm Android BlurTargetView / blurTarget; dimezisBlurViewSdk31Plus falls back without native blur below Android 12. Use explicit opaque tint for readability.
  • Retain Expo Router guards and native components. No DOM/Tailwind port, new frontend framework, backend mutation, new care feature or local cycle inference. Mockup navigation is a browser visualization only.

Direction selected.

Bloom Glass + subtle sage, selected by the owner. Keep the first direction’s layout, typography, spacing and warm palette; carry over the third direction’s crisp glass rims and surface distinction. The refinement applies to the phase anchor, supporting panels and floating dock.

This exports a local viewing note. The approved direction remains Bloom Glass + subtle sage with clearer glass borders; exploring another reference does not replace that selection.
